## Legs: run vs queued

### The engineering legs — RAN

- `ops/src/ops/post_cutover_probe.py` (new): the read-only probe.
  `ProbeRunner` protocol + `LiveRunner` (executes only argv that passes
  `argv_is_readonly` — dig/curl -sSI+curl -sS/openssl s_client+x509
  -noout/gcloud ssl-certificates describe/whois; a mutating argv raises,
  pinned by tests) + `CaptureRunner` (replays a capture directory — the
  same format `--capture` writes and the committed fixtures carry).
  Parsers for dig answer/flags/status blocks, curl HEAD status+headers,
  openssl x509 dates+SAN, gcloud JSON, WHOIS `Domain Status:` lines.
  `run_probe(leg="l1"|"l2")` emits a `sig.probe-run/1` record.
- `ops/src/ops/cli.py`: the `sig-ops post-cutover-probe` verb —
  `--leg l1|l2`, `--capture <dir>`, `--from-capture <dir>`, `--out`,
  `--domain`/`--expected-ip`/`--cert`/`--project` with
  `SIG_WEB_DOMAIN`/`SIG_WEB_EXPECTED_IP`/`SIG_LB_CERT`/`SIG_GCP_PROJECT`
  env defaults (the staging-endpoint seam, HG-12 convention). Exit 0 on
  pass/partial, 1 on fail.
- `docs/build/reports/POST_CUTOVER_PROBE_CHECKLIST.md` (new): the
  committed checklist — every L1/L2 check mapped to the runbook
  post-switch step it discharges, the exact read, and the pass
  condition; the runbook's grey-cloud rule lands as the Cloudflare
  anycast-address refusal inside `apex_a`/`www_a`; the OP-10 mail
  posture is a two-state check (`no_mail` pre-OP-10 / `op10_configured`
  — MX-without-SPF or SPF-without-MX fails), not a pin on the pre-alias
  state.
- `tests/ops/fixtures/post_cutover/precutover/`: the real
  2026-10-10T04:42Z capture of the still-Squarespace zone (labelled —
  it is a fixture for the parser/check tests, never post-cutover
  evidence); `good/`: the expected post-cutover capture shape for
  fixture tests (same format, synthesised DNSSEC/NS/MX answers).
- `tests/ops/test_post_cutover_probe.py` (44 tests): the read-only

## Deviations

- The deployed origin answers `sitemap.xml`/`sitemap-index.xml`
  404 — the `routes` check falls back to the `ops/public_routes.toml`
  allowlist rather than failing on a sitemap the origin never served;
  the fallback is named in the record (`route_source`).
- `www_redirect`/`http_redirect` Location headers carry an explicit
  `:443` port (`https://surveillancegraph.org:443/`) — the checker
  normalises default ports before comparing (an equivalent target, not
  a laxer check).
- CI repair chain recorded, not smoothed: impl head `572a08b7` failed
  the `security` job — the OP-07 leak check found the real GCP project
  id in the fixture `gcloud_cert.txt` `selfLink` URLs (scrubbed to the
  synthetic `sig-project-fixture` in `646a3985`); that head failed the
  `python` job — the future-date sweep scans **tracked** files, so the
  still-untracked new files had escaped the local run and CI caught 12
  literals across the probe, tests and comment-less JSON/WHOIS captures
  (`future-ok: scheduled:` markers where the format permits + expiring
  `history.policy` allow entries for the captures, in `4dfa114c`).
